**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity (name, school, parents, family background etc). You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **b)** Describe the installation ceremony of a very important personality in your area.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduce the personality (the new Paramount Chief) and the date and place.
2. Preparations in the village in the days before.
3. Arrival of the guests and the ceremony itself (dances, rites, speeches).
4. The oath, the symbols of power and the feast.
5. Conclusion: what the ceremony meant to the people.

**Model composition (481 words)**

The installation of Fon Ngwa III as the new Paramount Chief of my village was the most colourful event I have ever witnessed. It took place on a bright Saturday morning in December, in the large palace square, in the presence of thousands of people.

Preparations began a week before the great day. The women swept the village and the road leading to the palace, the young men cut grass and built wooden shelters for the guests, and the notables met every evening to plan the programme. On the eve of the ceremony, drums echoed throughout the village, announcing that something important was about to happen.

From early morning, people poured into the palace square wearing traditional robes of many colours. Dancers in beautiful costumes entertained the crowd, and the sound of drums, flutes and gongs filled the air. At about ten o'clock, a convoy of cars arrived, carrying the Divisional Officer, the Mayor, several Members of Parliament and chiefs from neighbouring villages. They were welcomed with songs and led to the seats of honour under a large white tent.

The ceremony proper began with a prayer led by the village elder, who thanked God and the ancestors for their blessings. Then the notables, dressed in long gowns and red caps, brought the new chief from the sacred house. He wore a gown covered with beads and a crown of feathers, and he held a carved wooden staff. The crowd rose to its feet and clapped, while the women shouted with joy.

The Divisional Officer read the official decree confirming him as the chief, and the head of the notables asked him to take the oath. In a loud voice, the new Fon promised to protect his people, to settle quarrels with justice, to respect the traditions of the land and to work for the development of the village. After the oath, he was seated on the royal stool, the symbol of his authority, and the elders poured palm wine on the ground as a sign of blessing.

Several speeches followed. The Mayor promised to support the chief in building a new health centre, and the president of the youth association asked him to guide them with wisdom. The chief thanked everyone and invited all to join the feast.

The rest of the day was devoted to eating, drinking and dancing. Huge pots of achu, ndole and rice were served, and the masquerades danced until the sun went down.

For us, the ceremony was not only a celebration. It reminded everybody of our rich culture and the unity of our people. In the evening, as I walked home with my family, my feet were tired and my voice was hoarse from clapping and singing, but my heart was full. I felt proud of my origin, and I promised myself that I would always respect and defend the customs of my people.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | A real description of the ceremony (preparations, guests, rites, speeches, feast), with details and a logical order in clear paragraphs |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Telling a story or giving a list of events instead of describing the ceremony with sensory details.
2. Choosing a personality and an area, but giving no names, places or details, so the description stays vague.
